route: hcube — bottom-antipodal walks on LP orientations of cubes: Klee–Minty, Amenta–Ziegler deformed products, Holt–Klee, and one-player realisability
headline: Every Amenta–Ziegler deformed product is bottom-antipodally flat — BA height at most the sum of its factors' heights, so at most d for Klee–Minty, Chvátal's form, Goldfarb–Sit and every deformed cube — which closes the classical geometric arsenal as a source for the pivot; h*_HK(5) = 11 is now verified (exhaustive at L = 12, explicit witness at L = 11); the blow-up's Holt–Klee failure is localised to two explicit 2-face conditions, one of which is intrinsic to the seed and fails for every height-maximal seed at m ≤ 4; and exact nondegenerate one-player games give h*_1(3..6) ≥ 4, 6, 9, 12.

results.name: hcube:rigid + hcube:dprod (THE MAIN THEOREM)
results.statement: Let P = P_1 ⋉ … ⋉ P_k be an Amenta–Ziegler deformed product (each factor's inequalities perturbed on the right-hand side by an affine function of the earlier factors' variables, the face lattice being the product's) in which each factor P_i is a polytope combinatorially an m_i-cube, so P is combinatorially the d-cube, d = Σ m_i; let c be a linear objective generic on P. Then h_BA(P,c) ≤ Σ_i h*_LP(m_i) ≤ Σ_i h*_HK(m_i). In particular a deformed CUBE (all m_i = 1) has h_BA ≤ d, and a deformed product of quadrilaterals has h_BA ≤ d. Supporting lemma: the fibre of P over a fixed choice of vertices in the first k−1 factors is a polytope with the SAME NORMAL FAN as P_k, so a fixed functional induces the same orientation on every fibre; the last block therefore evolves autonomously under the bottom-antipodal step.
results.argument: Lemma: fixing vertices w_1..w_{k−1} determines y_{<k} affinely (each factor simple, product face lattice), so the fibre is {y_k : C_k y_k ≤ d_k + D_k y_{<k}(w)} — same facet normals C_k, same face lattice, hence the same normal fan as P_k. An edge of P_k is the intersection of n_k − 1 facets, so its direction spans ker{C_r : r in T}, a line depending only on C_k; and the far endpoint satisfies the relaxed constraint strictly, which fixes the sign of the multiple. So sign(c_k·(q_1−q_0)) is the same in P_k and in every fibre: one fixed orientation σ_k. Theorem: the last block of s(y) is σ_k(w_k(y)), so w_k ↦ w_k ⊕ σ_k(w_k) autonomously; after at most H_k = h_BA(σ_k) ≤ h*_LP(m_k) steps it sits at σ_k's sink and never leaves. The walk is then confined to the face G = {w_k = sink}. At every vertex of G the tight constraints of block k are exactly the m_k tight at that sink, so the other block-k constraints are strict on G, and the m_k tight ones express y_k affinely in y_{<k}. The projection π of G to the first k−1 blocks is affine and injective and carries the vertices of G bijectively onto the vertices of P_1 ⋉ … ⋉ P_{k−1} (same recursion, same constraints), so π(G) = P_1 ⋉ … ⋉ P_{k−1}; the objective becomes c_{<k}·y_{<k} + c_k·y_k(y_{<k}), linear. Induction. (That LP orientations of cube-polytopes are AUSOs is the standard argument: on each face the objective has a unique minimiser, which is the face's unique sink, and the objective strictly decreases along the orientation.)
results.verification: hc_deform.py, hc_dprod.py, t_deform.py, t_deform2.py, t_dprod.py, t_dprod2.py — exact rationals. 210 deformed products of k = 2,3,4 quadrilaterals, each CERTIFIED to be a polytope with the product's face lattice (every one of the 4^k candidate vertices feasible with exactly 2k tight constraints; every edge, obtained by relaxing one tight constraint, blocked by exactly that constraint's partner and landing on the expected cube neighbour — so pointed with all edges bounded, hence bounded): all were AUSO and Holt–Klee, the last factor's fibre orientation was constant over every base vertex (0 violations), the last block was autonomous under the BA step (0 violations), and h ≤ h(σ_k) + h(sink face) held with 0 violations. For deformed cubes the last coordinate was uniform and the sink facet was again a deformed cube with the induced objective, 0 violations over several thousand random instances in dimensions 2–7, and the bound d was never exceeded (asserted in code).

results.name: hcube:km — the classical cubes measured
results.statement: In exact rational arithmetic: the Klee–Minty cube (ε = 1/4 and 1/10, d = 2..12), Chvátal's form of it (d = 2..10), and the Goldfarb–Sit rescaling (d = 2..12) all induce acyclic unique sink orientations whose longest directed path has 2^d − 1 edges (a HAMILTONIAN monotone path — this is why the classical pivot rules are exponential on them) and whose bottom-antipodal height is exactly d. For Klee–Minty the outmap is s(b) = { i : b_i ≡ b_{i+1} + … + b_d (mod 2) }, independent of ε ∈ (0,1/2), with sink (0,…,0,1). So the bound of hcube:dprod is attained, and the whole classical arsenal is LP-hard and BA-trivial.
results.argument: Each family is written as a deformed cube l_i(x_<i) ≤ x_i ≤ u_i(x_<i); vertices computed recursively in Fractions; the orientation read off the 2^d exact objective values; longest monotone path by topological DP. The Goldfarb–Sit entry is my reconstruction from memory (the Klee–Minty cube with the variables diagonally rescaled) and is flagged as such in the write-up; a nonsingular diagonal rescaling of the variables does not change the objective values at vertices, so the LP orientation is Klee–Minty's — and in any case hcube:dprod covers every deformed cube whatever the constants.
results.verification: hc_deform.py + t_deform.py (table printed; the KM outmap identity checked against the objective values for d ≤ 8; Holt–Klee verified for d ≤ 6).

results.name: hcube:hkfive — h*_HK(5) = 11
results.statement: No Holt–Klee acyclic unique sink orientation of the 5-cube has a bottom-antipodal walk of length 12, and one has a walk of length 11. An explicit witness is s = (7,14,28,13,24,25,26,27,15,16,17,22,19,4,5,18,30,29,0,31,3,10,12,9,23,2,8,1,11,20,21,6), with walk 0,7,28,23,30,11,29,9,25,27,26,18. Hence h*_HK(m) = 1,2,4,6,11 for m = 1..5, against h*(m) = 1,2,4,7,12.
results.argument: Both laws (cor:no-return, cor:law-b) are translation invariant, so σ_0 = 0. All 347640 law-abiding sequences of length 12 were enumerated (the count agrees with hstar5.log); for each, the outmap was fixed on the 13 trace vertices and completed over the remaining 19 by DFS under the Szabó–Welzl condition, pruned as soon as a fully assigned face of dimension 3 or 4 failed acyclicity, the unique source/sink test, or the Holt–Klee disjoint-path count. The prune is sound: every face of a Holt–Klee AUSO is acyclic, has a unique sink (USO) and a unique source (the reversal of a USO is a USO), and is Holt–Klee. Zero completions survived. Controls: with the prune off, the same program reproduces prop:hstar-five's height-12 witness outmap (15,0,1,2,27,30,12,…) from the same trace 0,15,24,31,20,23,18,… — an exact match with the root agent's independent program; and at m = 4 it returns 168 completions / 48 acyclic at L = 7 with the prune off and 0 with it on, reproducing h*_HK(4) = 6.
results.verification: hc_hk.c (compiled hc_hk; runs logged in logs/hk5_L12.log and the transcript), t_wit5.py (independent Python re-verification of the witness: bijection, USO on all 496 pairs, acyclic, heights, max 11, Holt–Klee on all 51 faces of dimension ≥ 3). The max-flow test itself (hc_cube.py, unit vertex capacities, Ford–Fulkerson with BFS augmentation and residual arcs) was validated in t_validate.py: 12 USOs of the 2-cube all acyclic and Holt–Klee; 744 / 728 (18 classes) / 656 (16 classes) on the 3-cube — matching prop:auso-census exactly; and on G#'s height-7 orientation it returns 2 paths where 4 are needed, failing on the 3-face with directions {1,2,4} at vertex 4, exactly the face cor:seven-two-player names.

results.name: hcube:stack — the two stacking rules
results.statement: Stack two 2-cube USOs F (top) and G (bottom) with the vertical edge at v pointing up iff φ(v) = 1. (a) If G = F the result is always a USO, and over all 12·16 = 192 pairs (F,φ) it is acyclic and Holt–Klee in exactly 168: precisely when it is NOT the case that φ is balanced (|φ^{-1}(1)| = 2) and φ(src F) = φ(snk F). (b) If φ ≡ 0 (all verticals down) all 12·12 = 144 pairs are acyclic USOs and exactly 16 fail Holt–Klee: precisely when both F and G have source adjacent to sink and the two source–sink edges are opposite edges of the square.
results.argument: Exhaustion over all 12 USOs of the 2-cube and all 16 maps φ (resp. all 12·12 pairs), with the certified max-flow test on every face.
results.verification: t_stack.py, t_stack2.py — both rules confirmed as exact iff-statements with zero exceptions.

results.name: hcube:blowfaces — where thm:blowup loses Holt–Klee
results.statement: For B(s,z), let F be the 2-face of s on directions {i,j} at base v̄ and G the orientation v ↦ s(v⊕z) read on the same square. (i) The 3-face on {i,j,α} with β = 1 is the stack of F over F with φ = h mod 2, and the one on {i,j,β} with α = 1 is the same stack with 1 − φ. (ii) The 3-faces on {i,j,α} with β = 0 and on {i,j,β} with α = 0 are the stack of F over G with all verticals pointing to layer (0,0). Consequently B(s,z) is Holt–Klee ONLY IF for every 2-face F: (P) h mod 2 is not balanced on F, or h(src F) ≢ h(snk F) mod 2; and (T) F and G do not both have source adjacent to sink with opposite source–sink edges.
results.argument: Direct from thm:blowup's table of O_{αβ}: O_{01} contains α iff h(v) is odd and O_{11} contains α iff h(v) is even, so the α-edge between layers (0,1) and (1,1) points up iff h(v) is odd; O_{10} contains β iff h(v) is even and O_{11} iff odd, so the β-edge between (1,0) and (1,1) points up iff h(v) is even — that is (i). O_{00} = ∅ while both parities of O_{10} contain α and both of O_{01} contain β, so those α- and β-edges all point to layer (0,0) uniformly — that is (ii). Then apply hcube:stack; Holt–Klee is inherited by faces.
results.verification: hc_blowhk.py builds the kind-(II) and kind-(III) 3-faces directly from (s,h,z); t_blowhk.py and t_blowhk2.py check the prediction against the direct max-flow test on B(s,z) for the 1-cube seed, all 2 classes of the 2-cube and all 18 of the 3-cube (69 instances): 'no predicted bad 3-face' agreed with 'Holt–Klee' in 68 of 69, the one exception being an orientation with all 3-faces good and a 4-face bad — which is why the conditions are stated as NECESSARY only. It also reproduces the paper's fact that exactly four of the eight height-2 seeds of the 2-cube give a Holt–Klee B, and identifies the six failing 3-faces of B² = B(B(1-cube)) exactly (one of kind (P), two of kind (T), each doubled).

results.name: hcube:parity — the parity obstruction is a property of the seed alone
results.statement: Condition (P) does not involve z. Call s parity-good when (P) holds on every 2-face. Then: at m = 3, no class of height 4 is parity-good and the greatest height of a parity-good class is 3 (14 of the 18 classes are parity-good); at m = 4, of the 12640 classes the unique class of height 7 is NOT parity-good, and of the 56 Holt–Klee classes of height 6 exactly 15 are. Hence for a height-maximal seed at m = 3 or m = 4, B(s,z) fails Holt–Klee for EVERY z.
results.argument: (P) is read off h mod 2 and the source/sink of each 2-face and mentions z nowhere; the census is an exhaustive scan of one representative of every isomorphism class (enumerated for m ≤ 3, taken from census/classes4.txt for m = 4).
results.verification: hc_blowhk.py (parity_good), t_blowhk2.py — full table by height and Holt–Klee status: heights 1..7 give parity-good counts 1/1, 155/331 + 302/423, 989/2273 + 1489/2503, 1379/3003 + 1113/2401, 175/832 + 261/729, 16/87 + 15/56, 0/1.

results.name: hcube:transl — the translation obstruction, and why B² is never Holt–Klee
results.statement: If z = e_i is a single coordinate and B(s,e_i) satisfies (T) on every 2-face containing direction i, then coordinate i is UNIFORM in s. Moreover no outer coordinate of a blow-up is ever uniform. Hence the second and every later iterate of B fails Holt–Klee whenever its translation vector is a single outer coordinate of the previous level — which rem:blowup-measured records that it is.
results.argument: For z = e_i and a 2-face on {i,j}, G is F translated by the local i-coordinate, so {src G, snk G} = {src F ⊕ e_i, snk F ⊕ e_i}; the two pairs are disjoint exactly when src F and snk F are adjacent along j. A 2-face of a USO has src and snk adjacent along j iff its two i-edges point in opposite ways (case check over the three possibilities: adjacent along i, adjacent along j, antipodal). So (T) on all faces containing i makes the i-edge orientation constant on each facet {v_i = 0}, {v_i = 1}, i.e. i is uniform. For the second sentence: the α-edge between layers (0,1) and (1,1) points up exactly at the v of odd height, while the α-edge between (0,0) and (1,0) always points to (0,0); h takes both parities on every cube with a non-sink vertex, so α is not uniform, and symmetrically for β.
results.verification: t_zcor2.py: 50618 (seed, coordinate) pairs over all classes of dimension 2, 3 and all 12640 of dimension 4 — 6133 have no kind-(IIa/IIc) failure and in every one of those the coordinate is uniform, 0 counterexamples; and over 59688 blow-ups an outer coordinate is uniform in 0 of them.

results.name: hcube:blowbest — how high a Holt–Klee blow-up can go
results.statement: Over every AUSO class of the m-cube for m ≤ 3 and every one of the 2^m translation vectors z, the Holt–Klee blow-ups B(s,z) have greatest bottom-antipodal height 4, 6, 8 at dimensions 3, 4, 5 — always 2h+2 with h the greatest height of a parity-good seed of that dimension. Against h*_HK = 4, 6, 11 this means B meets the Holt–Klee ceiling at dimensions 3 and 4 and falls three short at 5; over these dimensions its growth inside the Holt–Klee class is +2 per dimension, i.e. LINEAR. The twisted product of lem:hstar-super is no better: of the 288 twisted products of a 2-cube with a 3-cube orientation, 186 are not Holt–Klee and the tallest Holt–Klee one has height 5; twisting the 1-cube against the height-11 witness gives Holt–Klee height at most 11 at dimension 6, attained only by the untwisted product.
results.argument: Exhaustive scan over class representatives and all z, filtering by the necessary conditions (P),(T) and then by the direct max-flow Holt–Klee test on the (m+2)-cube.
results.verification: t_zcor2.py (dimensions 1→3, 2→4, 3→5 complete; the 4→6 scan over all 12640 classes × 16 translations was still running when this report was written, output going to logs/zcor2.log), t_super.py (the twisted-product measurements).

results.name: hcube:oneplayer — explicit nondegenerate one-player runs
results.argument: Simulated annealing on the integer rows, scored by the all-switches run length with the mean height as a smooth tie-break; floats to search, Fractions to certify. This is NOT random sampling: it recovers the exact optima 4 at m = 3 and 6 at m = 4 in seconds, which is the calibration. The larger values are lower bounds and are not claimed tight. Rounds are counted as productive all-switches rounds with the STRICT switchable set.
results.verification: hc_climb2.py + hc_one.py + t_records.py. Every reported game was re-solved in exact rationals: substochastic rows with a strict leak (hence stopping), ties = 0, run length recomputed, and — as an independent check on prop:oneplayer-lp — each improvement orientation was verified to be a USO, acyclic and Holt–Klee. The pipeline was validated by reloading the root agent's AP_m4_k0_den256_s200 game and reproducing its outmap, ties = 0 and run length 6 exactly.

results.name: hcube:lp4 — LP realisability as an explicit criterion, and a dyadic realisation
results.statement: An orientation s of the m-cube is the orientation induced by a linear objective on a polytope combinatorially an m-cube iff there are affine forms f_{v,a}(x) = b_{v,a} − A_{v,a}·x and a vector c with (i) f_{v,1−σ(v)}(x_σ) > 0 for every σ and v, where x_σ solves A_{v,σ(v)}·x = b_{v,σ(v)}; (ii) no other m-subset of the 2m forms has a feasible basic solution and the recession cone {d : A_{v,a}·d ≤ 0 ∀ v,a} is trivial; (iii) c separates the ends of every cube edge and orients them as s. The Holt–Klee class of height 6 at m = 4 realised by AP_m4_k0_den256_s200 admits such a realisation with dyadic data of denominator 64 (matrices printed in the write-up and in LP_m4_s2.json).
results.argument: (i) makes each x_σ a nondegenerate vertex of P (exactly m tight constraints, all others strict); (ii) rules out any other vertex and any extreme ray, so P is a polytope with exactly the 2^m points x_σ as vertices, simple, with 2m facets in m opposite pairs; relaxing one tight constraint moves along an edge whose only possible blocker is that constraint's partner (two tight constraints from one pair would be a degenerate vertex), so the graph is the m-cube; (iii) is the LP orientation. The realisation was found by smooth hinge minimisation from the standard cube and then certified exactly in Fractions: all 16 transversal points feasible with exactly four tight constraints, all C(8,4) − 16 = 54 other bases infeasible or singular, no extreme ray of the recession cone, no tied edge, orientation equal to the target.
results.verification: hc_lp.py (fit + exact certification), LP_m4_s2.json. Control: the same program, run on G#'s non-Holt–Klee height-7 orientation, fails as it must.

results.name: hcube:notdeformed — occupancy polytopes are outside the deformed-product world
results.statement: The improvement orientation of a nondegenerate one-player stopping game with |Vmax| = 4 and an all-switches run of length 6 is NOT the LP orientation of any deformed cube.
results.argument: By hcube:dprod's proof, a deformed cube's LP orientation has a uniform coordinate. A uniform coordinate forces h_BA ≤ 1 + h*(m−1), since one bottom-antipodal step carries every vertex into the facet the coordinate points to and the walk never leaves it. At m = 4 that ceiling is 1 + h*(3) = 5 < 6.
results.verification: h*(3) = 4 is prop:auso-census; the length-6 one-player games are hcube:oneplayer, certified exactly in t_records.py.

results.name: hcube:five — the five unresolved Holt–Klee classes at m = 4
results.argument: The one-player search (realiseAP, fresh seeds, 1500 s + repair, two seeds each) plateaued near hinge 4e−3 on all five and never closed. The weaker LP-realisability search (hc_lp.py, 900 s and 2000 s runs) also plateaued on all five. But that second search is NOT a discriminator: run on ten control classes that the survey did realise by one-player games — hence LP orientations by prop:oneplayer-lp — it closed on only one within the same budget. So no conclusion may be drawn, and I explicitly do not claim these five are unrealisable. Recorded honestly in the write-up as rem:hcube-five, with the exact missing statement as (G2).
results.verification: logs/u4_*.log (one-player), logs/lpA..E.log, logs/lpA2..E2.log (LP), logs/lpctl_1..10.log (the ten controls).

gap: (G1) For every m ≥ 1, h*_HK(m+2) ≥ 2·h*_HK(m) + 2 — that is, there is an operation carrying a Holt–Klee acyclic unique sink orientation of the m-cube of maximal bottom-antipodal height to a Holt–Klee acyclic unique sink orientation of the (m+2)-cube of bottom-antipodal height at least twice that plus two. (It holds for m ≤ 3, since h*_HK(5) = 11 ≥ 2·4+2; thm:blowup's B does not witness it, by hcube:parity and hcube:transl; no witness is known. This is the exact statement whose truth would make an LP-realisable — and, if the m = 4 coincidence of Holt–Klee with one-player realisability persists, a ONE-PLAYER — exponential all-switches family the next construction to build, and whose failure would be the first genuine ceiling on the one-player half of the pivot.)

\section{Bottom-antipodal walks on deformed cubes}\label{sec:hcube}

\Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp} turns the one-player half of the pivot into a question
about polytopes: for a nondegenerate one-player stopping game the improvement
orientation is the orientation a linear objective induces on a simple
$m$-polytope with the graph of the $m$-cube, all-switches is the
bottom-antipodal walk of that orientation, and every such orientation is
Holt--Klee. The classical source of long simplex paths on cubes is the
Klee--Minty cube and its descendants, and \Cref{rem:blowup-measured} already
records that the Klee--Minty cube has bottom-antipodal height exactly $d$. This
section explains why, and the explanation covers the whole family.

\begin{definition}[Deformed products; Amenta--Ziegler]\label{def:hcube-deformed}
Let $P_i=\{y_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}:C_iy_i\le d_i\}$ be polytopes,
$i=1,\dots,k$, and let $D_i$ be matrices. The \emph{deformed product}
$P_1\ltimes\cdots\ltimes P_k$ is
\[
  P:=\bigl\{y=(y_1,\dots,y_k)\ :\ C_iy_i\le d_i+D_i(y_1,\dots,y_{i-1}),
     \ i=1,\dots,k\bigr\},
\]
assumed to be a polytope whose face lattice is that of $P_1\times\cdots\times
P_k$, the facet of $P$ cut by the $r$-th row of the $i$-th block corresponding
to the facet of $P_i$ cut by the $r$-th row of $C_i$. When every $P_i$ is a
segment this is a \emph{deformed cube}: after normalising,
\[
  P=\bigl\{x\in\mathbb R^{d}\ :\ l_i(x_1,\dots,x_{i-1})\le x_i\le
    u_i(x_1,\dots,x_{i-1}),\ i=1,\dots,d\bigr\}
\]
with $l_i,u_i$ affine and $l_i<u_i$ on $P$; its vertices are indexed by
$b\in\{0,1\}^{d}$, with $x_i=u_i$ if $b_i=1$ and $x_i=l_i$ if $b_i=0$, computed
recursively. The Klee--Minty cube
$0\le x_1\le1$, $\varepsilon x_{i-1}\le x_i\le1-\varepsilon x_{i-1}$ with
objective $x_d$; Chv\'atal's form
$2\sum_{j<i}10^{i-j}x_j+x_i\le100^{i-1}$, $x\ge0$, with objective
$\sum_j10^{d-j}x_j$; and the Goldfarb--Sit cube, which is the Klee--Minty cube
with the variables rescaled, are all deformed cubes.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[The last factor is rigid]\label{lem:hcube-rigid}
Let $P=P_1\ltimes\cdots\ltimes P_k$ be a deformed product with each $P_i$ a
simple $n_i$-polytope, and fix vertices $w_1,\dots,w_{k-1}$ of the first $k-1$
factors. The fibre of $P$ over $(w_1,\dots,w_{k-1})$ projects isomorphically
onto
$Q(w):=\{y_k:C_ky_k\le d_k+D_k(y_{<k}(w))\}$, and $Q(w)$ has the same normal
fan as $P_k$. Consequently, for each edge of the combinatorial cube of $P_k$
the vector joining its two endpoints in $Q(w)$ is a positive multiple of the
corresponding vector in $P_k$; so a fixed linear functional $c_k$ induces the
\emph{same} orientation on every fibre.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The face lattice of $P$ being the product's, at a point of the fibre the tight
constraints of the first $k-1$ blocks are exactly those tight at
$w_1,\dots,w_{k-1}$; each block being simple, those determine $y_i$ as an affine
function of $y_{<i}$, so $y_{<k}$ is the constant $y_{<k}(w)$ and the fibre is
$\{y_k:C_ky_k\le d_k+D_k(y_{<k}(w))\}$, which is $Q(w)$.

$Q(w)$ and $P_k$ are cut by the same normal vectors --- the rows of $C_k$ ---
and have the same face lattice with the same labelling of facets, so their
normal fans coincide. Let $e$ be an edge of $P_k$ with endpoints $q_0,q_1$,
where $q_a$ carries the tight facets $T\cup\{j_a\}$, $|T|=n_k-1$. In both
polytopes the direction of $e$ spans $\ker\{C_r:r\in T\}$, a line depending only
on $C_k$; and the endpoint $q_1$ satisfies $C_{j_0}q_1<d_{j_0}$, so the sign of
the multiple is fixed by $C_{j_0}$, again independent of $w$. Hence
$\operatorname{sign}\bigl(c_k\cdot(q_1-q_0)\bigr)$ is the same in $P_k$ and in
$Q(w)$, for every edge.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Deformed products are bottom-antipodally flat]\label{thm:hcube-dprod}
Let $P=P_1\ltimes\cdots\ltimes P_k$ be a deformed product in which each factor
$P_i$ is a polytope combinatorially equivalent to the $m_i$-cube, so that $P$ is
combinatorially the $d$-cube with $d=\sum_im_i$, and let $c$ be a linear
objective taking distinct values at the two ends of every edge of $P$. Then the
bottom-antipodal height of the orientation $s$ that $c$ induces on $P$ satisfies
\[
  h_{\mathrm{BA}}(P,c)\ \le\ \sum_{i=1}^{k}h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{LP}}(m_i)
   \ \le\ \sum_{i=1}^{k}h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(m_i),
\]
where $h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{LP}}(m)$ denotes the greatest bottom-antipodal height
of an orientation induced by a linear objective on a polytope combinatorially
equivalent to the $m$-cube. In particular a deformed \emph{cube}
$(m_i=1$ for all $i)$ has $h_{\mathrm{BA}}\le d$, and a deformed product of
quadrilaterals $(m_i=2)$ has $h_{\mathrm{BA}}\le d$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
First, the orientation a generic linear objective induces on a polytope
combinatorially a cube is an acyclic unique sink orientation: on each face the
objective attains its minimum at a unique vertex, and from any other vertex of
that face some edge of the face decreases, so each face has a unique sink; and
the orientation is acyclic because the objective strictly decreases along it.
Hence all the orientations below have terminating bottom-antipodal walks.

Induction on $k$; for $k=0$ there is nothing to prove. Write $w_k(y)$ for the
last block's vertex label. By \Cref{lem:hcube-rigid} the last block of $s(y)$
is $\sigma_k(w_k(y))$ for a single orientation $\sigma_k$ of the $m_k$-cube,
independent of the other blocks, and $\sigma_k$ is the orientation induced by
$c_k$ on $P_k$, hence has a unique sink and bottom-antipodal height
$H_k\le h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{LP}}(m_k)$. The bottom-antipodal step
$y\mapsto y\oplus s(y)$ therefore acts on the last block autonomously,
$w_k\mapsto w_k\oplus\sigma_k(w_k)$: after at most $H_k$ steps the last block
sits at $\sigma_k$'s sink $w^{\ast}_k$, and it never leaves.

Let $G:=\{y\in P:w_k(y)=w^{\ast}_k\}$, a face of $P$. Once the walk is in $G$ it
stays there and each of its steps is the bottom-antipodal step of the
orientation induced on $G$. At every vertex of $G$ the tight constraints of the
last block are exactly the $m_k$ tight at $w^{\ast}_k$, so the remaining
constraints of the last block are strict at every vertex of $G$ and hence on
$G$; the $m_k$ tight ones express $y_k$ as an affine function of $y_{<k}$. So
the projection $\pi$ of $G$ to the first $k-1$ blocks is injective and affine,
and carries the vertices of $G$ --- one for each choice of vertices in the first
$k-1$ factors --- bijectively onto the vertices of
$P_1\ltimes\cdots\ltimes P_{k-1}$, which are computed by the same recursion from
the same constraints; two polytopes with the same vertex set are equal, so
$\pi(G)=P_1\ltimes\cdots\ltimes P_{k-1}$. Under $\pi$ the objective becomes the
linear functional $y_{<k}\mapsto c_{<k}\cdot y_{<k}+c_k\cdot y_k(y_{<k})$ up to
an additive constant. The induction hypothesis bounds the rest of the walk by
$\sum_{i<k}h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{LP}}(m_i)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:hcube-dprod-check}
The lemma and the theorem were checked directly. On $210$ deformed products of
$k=2,3,4$ quadrilaterals with random rational data --- each certified to be a
polytope with the product's face lattice by verifying that every one of the
$4^{k}$ candidate vertices is feasible with exactly $2k$ tight constraints and
that every edge, obtained by relaxing one tight constraint, is blocked by
precisely that constraint's partner and lands on the expected cube neighbour, so
that the polyhedron is pointed with all edges bounded and hence a polytope ---
every LP orientation was an acyclic unique sink orientation and Holt--Klee, the
orientation induced on the last factor's fibre was the same $2$-cube
orientation over every base vertex, the last block's coordinates evolved
autonomously under the bottom-antipodal step, and
$h_{\mathrm{BA}}\le h(\sigma_k)+h_{\mathrm{BA}}(\text{sink face})$ held with no
exception. On deformed cubes the last coordinate was uniform and the facet it
points to was again a deformed cube with the induced objective, with no
exception over several thousand random instances in dimensions $2$ to $7$, and
no instance ever exceeded the bound $d$.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[The classical cubes, measured]\label{prop:hcube-km}
In exact rational arithmetic, in the ranges of the table of
\Cref{rem:hcube-km}: the Klee--Minty cube with $\varepsilon\in\{1/4,1/10\}$,
Chv\'atal's form of it, and the Goldfarb--Sit
rescaling all induce acyclic unique sink orientations of the $d$-cube whose
longest directed path has $2^{d}-1$ edges --- it is a Hamiltonian monotone path,
which is why the classical pivot rules are exponential on them --- and whose
bottom-antipodal height is exactly $d$. For the Klee--Minty cube the outmap is
\[
  s(b)=\bigl\{\,i\ :\ b_i\equiv b_{i+1}+\cdots+b_d \pmod 2\,\bigr\},
\]
independently of $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$, with sink $(0,\dots,0,1)$; this was
checked against the objective values for $d\le8$. So on these cubes the
bound of \Cref{thm:hcube-dprod} is attained.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:hcube-km}
The table separates the two questions completely.
\[
\begin{array}{lccc}
\text{family} & d & \text{longest monotone path} & h_{\mathrm{BA}}\\ \hline
\text{Klee--Minty }(\varepsilon=1/4) & 2..12 & 2^{d}-1 & d\\
\text{Klee--Minty }(\varepsilon=1/10) & 2..12 & 2^{d}-1 & d\\
\text{Klee--Minty, Chv\'atal's form} & 2..10 & 2^{d}-1 & d\\
\text{Goldfarb--Sit rescaling} & 2..12 & 2^{d}-1 & d
\end{array}
\]
Every deformed cube is LP-hard-capable and bottom-antipodally trivial, and
\Cref{thm:hcube-dprod} says this is not an accident of the constants: it is
forced by the shape of the definition. A deformed product may only chain its
factors' \emph{heights} additively, so no family of deformed products with
factors of bounded dimension has superlinear bottom-antipodal height. Since
\Cref{def:hcube-deformed} is the standard machine for producing long monotone
paths on cubes --- Klee--Minty, Goldfarb, Goldfarb--Sit, and the
Amenta--Ziegler deformed products that give maximal shadows --- the whole
classical arsenal is useless for \Cref{cor:f-auso}'s pivot, and a
superpolynomial all-switches family must be built by something else. The
attribution of \Cref{def:hcube-deformed} to Amenta and Ziegler, and of the
cubes to Klee and Minty, to Chv\'atal, and to Goldfarb and Sit, is from memory
and unchecked against the sources; the theorem does not depend on the constants
of any particular one of them.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:hcube-notallcubes}
\Cref{thm:hcube-dprod} does not apply to the occupancy polytope $X(G)$ of
\Cref{prop:oneplayer-lp}, and it must not. The proof produces, in every deformed
product, a block of coordinates on which the orientation does not depend on the
rest; for a deformed \emph{cube} that block is a single \emph{uniform}
coordinate, all of whose edges point the same way. A uniform coordinate forces
$h_{\mathrm{BA}}\le1+h^{\ast}(m-1)$, because one bottom-antipodal step carries
every vertex into the facet the coordinate points to and the walk never leaves
it. At $m=4$ that ceiling is $1+h^{\ast}(3)=5$, whereas one-player stopping
games with $|\Vmax|=4$ and an all-switches run of length $6$ exist
(\Cref{prop:hcube-oneplayer}). So their improvement orientation is not the LP
orientation of any deformed cube, and the geometry of $X(G)$ is genuinely
outside \Cref{def:hcube-deformed}.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[$h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(5)=11$]\label{prop:hcube-hkfive}
No Holt--Klee acyclic unique sink orientation of the $5$-cube has a
bottom-antipodal walk of length $12$, and some Holt--Klee acyclic unique sink
orientation of the $5$-cube has one of length $11$; an explicit witness is
\[
  \begin{aligned}
  s=(&7,14,28,13,24,25,26,27,15,16,17,22,19,4,5,18,\\
     &30,29,0,31,3,10,12,9,23,2,8,1,11,20,21,6),
  \end{aligned}
\]
whose bottom-antipodal walk from $\sigma_0=0$ is
$0,7,28,23,30,11,29,9,25,27,26,18$. Hence
\[
  h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(m)=1,\;2,\;4,\;6,\;11\qquad(m=1,\dots,5),
\]
against $h^{\ast}(m)=1,2,4,7,12$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By \Cref{lem:auso-laws} every bottom-antipodal trace obeys \Cref{cor:no-return}
and \Cref{cor:law-b}, and both laws are translation invariant, so
$\sigma_0=0$ may be assumed. The $347640$ law-abiding sequences of length $12$
on the $5$-cube were enumerated as in \Cref{prop:hstar-five}; for each, the
outmap was fixed on the $13$ vertices of the trace and completed over the
remaining $19$ by depth-first search under the Szab\'o--Welzl condition, with a
prune firing as soon as a face of dimension $3$ or $4$ became fully assigned
and failed acyclicity, the unique source/sink condition, or the Holt--Klee
count of internally vertex-disjoint monotone source-to-sink paths. The prune is
sound: every face of a Holt--Klee acyclic unique sink orientation is acyclic,
has a unique sink, has a unique source (the reversal of a unique sink
orientation is one), and is Holt--Klee. No completion survived. The same
program with the Holt--Klee prune switched off reproduces
\Cref{prop:hstar-five}'s witness outmap $(15,0,1,2,27,30,12,\dots)$ from the
same trace $0,15,24,31,20,23,18,\dots$, which is the check on the enumeration;
with the prune on and length $11$ it returns the displayed orientation after
$73266$ sequences. That orientation was then re-verified independently: the
outmap is a bijection, the Szab\'o--Welzl condition holds on all $496$ pairs,
the orientation is acyclic, its bottom-antipodal heights are
$(11,7,8,8,10,10,10,10,11,4,3,6,5,5,7,6,8,6,0,6,9,5,2,8,7,3,1,2,9,5,7,4)$ with
maximum $11$, and the Holt--Klee maximum flow succeeds on all $51$ faces of
dimension at least three (the $2$-faces of a unique sink orientation are
automatic).

The Holt--Klee test is a unit vertex-capacity maximum flow computed by
Ford--Fulkerson with breadth-first augmentation and residual arcs on the
vertex-split graph of each face. It was validated by recomputing, from an
independent enumeration, the census of \Cref{prop:auso-census}: $12$ unique
sink orientations of the $2$-cube, all acyclic and all Holt--Klee; $744$ of the
$3$-cube, $728$ acyclic in $18$ classes, $656$ Holt--Klee in $16$ classes; and
on the orientation of \Cref{prop:auso-seven} it returns $2$ disjoint paths
where $4$ are needed, with the same failing $3$-face (directions $1,2,4$ at the
vertex $4$) that \Cref{cor:seven-two-player} names.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:hcube-hkfive}
This confirms the measurement recorded as unverified. Two consequences. First,
$h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}$ is not merely $h^{\ast}$ with the top removed: it loses
one at $m=4$ and one at $m=5$, and the losses are independent computations.
Second, the numbers leave room for a doubling: $11\ge2\cdot4+2$, so nothing in
the table forbids an operation raising the dimension by two and at least
doubling the height \emph{inside} the Holt--Klee class, which is what an
LP-realisable exponential family would need. \Cref{sec:hcube-blow} shows that
\Cref{thm:blowup}'s $B$ is not such an operation and says exactly which face
stops it.
\end{remark}

\section{Why the blow-up leaves the Holt--Klee class}\label{sec:hcube-blow}

Fix an acyclic unique sink orientation $s$ of the $m$-cube with height function
$h$ and sink $o$, and a translation vector $z$; write $B=B(s,z)$ for
\Cref{thm:blowup}'s blow-up. Every $3$-face of $B$ is of one of three kinds:
three inner directions (a $3$-face of $s$ or of $s\circ\tau_z$, Holt--Klee
because $s$ is); two inner and one outer; one inner and two outer. The middle
kind is where $B$ fails, and it fails for two independent reasons.

\begin{lemma}[The two stacking rules]\label{lem:hcube-stack}
Let $F$ and $G$ be unique sink orientations of the $2$-cube and let
$\varphi:\{0,1\}^{2}\to\{0,1\}$; build the orientation of the $3$-cube whose
bottom copy $\{x_3=0\}$ carries $G$, whose top copy carries $F$, and whose
vertical edge at $v$ points up iff $\varphi(v)=1$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(a)] if $G=F$, the result is always a unique sink orientation, and over
  all $12\cdot16=192$ pairs $(F,\varphi)$ it is acyclic and Holt--Klee in
  exactly $168$ of them: precisely when it is \emph{not} the case that
  $\varphi$ is balanced $(|\varphi^{-1}(1)|=2)$ and
  $\varphi(\mathrm{src}\,F)=\varphi(\mathrm{snk}\,F)$;
\item[\rm(b)] if $\varphi\equiv0$, so that all vertical edges point down, all
  $12\cdot12=144$ pairs give an acyclic unique sink orientation, and exactly
  $16$ fail Holt--Klee: precisely when both $F$ and $G$ have their source
  adjacent to their sink and the two source-sink edges are opposite edges of
  the square.
\end{enumerate}
Both statements were verified by exhaustion with the max-flow test.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The $3$-faces of the blow-up]\label{lem:hcube-blowfaces}
Let $F$ be the $2$-face of $s$ with directions $\{i,j\}$ and base $\bar v$, and
let $G$ be the orientation $v\mapsto s(v\oplus z)$ read on the same square.
Then in $B(s,z)$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(i)] the $3$-face on $\{i,j,\alpha\}$ with $\beta=1$ is the stack of
  $F$ over $F$ with $\varphi(v)=h(v)\bmod2$, and the $3$-face on $\{i,j,\beta\}$
  with $\alpha=1$ is the same stack with $\varphi$ replaced by $1-\varphi$;
\item[\rm(ii)] the $3$-faces on $\{i,j,\alpha\}$ with $\beta=0$ and on
  $\{i,j,\beta\}$ with $\alpha=0$ are the stack of $F$ over $G$ with all
  vertical edges pointing towards the layer $(0,0)$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, $B(s,z)$ is Holt--Klee only if for every $2$-face $F$ of the
$m$-cube
\begin{itemize}
\item[\rm(P)] $h\bmod2$ is not balanced on $F$, or
  $h(\mathrm{src}\,F)\not\equiv h(\mathrm{snk}\,F)\pmod2$; and
\item[\rm(T)] $F$ and $G$ do not both have source adjacent to sink with
  opposite source-sink edges.
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The inner part of $B$ is $s$ on the three layers other than $(0,0)$ and
$s(\cdot\oplus z)$ on $(0,0)$, which gives the two stacks. For the outer part,
$O_{01}$ contains $\alpha$ exactly when $h(v)$ is odd and $O_{11}$ contains
$\alpha$ exactly when $h(v)$ is even, so the $\alpha$-edge between the layers
$(0,1)$ and $(1,1)$ points up exactly when $h(v)$ is odd; $O_{10}$ contains
$\beta$ exactly when $h(v)$ is even and $O_{11}$ contains $\beta$ exactly when
$h(v)$ is odd, so the $\beta$-edge between $(1,0)$ and $(1,1)$ points up exactly
when $h(v)$ is even. That is (i). $O_{00}=\emptyset$ while $O_{10}\supseteq
\{\alpha\}$ and $O_{01}\supseteq\{\beta\}$ for both parities, so the
$\alpha$-edges between $(0,0)$ and $(1,0)$, and the $\beta$-edges between
$(0,0)$ and $(0,1)$, all point towards the layer $(0,0)$, uniformly; that is
(ii). The two conditions are \Cref{lem:hcube-stack} read off these faces, and
Holt--Klee is inherited by faces.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The parity obstruction is intrinsic to the seed]%
\label{cor:hcube-parity}
Condition {\rm(P)} does not involve $z$. Call $s$ \emph{parity-good} when it
holds for every $2$-face. Among the acyclic unique sink orientations of the
$3$-cube, no class of height $4$ is parity-good and the greatest height of a
parity-good class is $3$; among the $12640$ classes of the $4$-cube the unique
class of height $7$ is not parity-good, and of the $56$ Holt--Klee classes of
height $6$ exactly $15$ are. So for a seed of maximal height at $m=3$ or $m=4$,
$B(s,z)$ fails Holt--Klee for every $z$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[The translation obstruction]\label{cor:hcube-transl}
If $z=e_i$ is a single coordinate and $B(s,e_i)$ satisfies condition {\rm(T)} on
every $2$-face containing the direction $i$, then coordinate $i$ is uniform in
$s$. Moreover neither outer coordinate of a blow-up is ever uniform, because the
$\alpha$-edge between the layers $(0,1)$ and $(1,1)$ points up exactly at the
$v$ of odd height and $h$ always takes both parities. Hence the second and
every later iterate of $B$ fails Holt--Klee whenever its translation vector is a
single outer coordinate of the previous level, which is what
\Cref{rem:blowup-measured} records that it is.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For $z=e_i$ and a $2$-face $F$ with directions $\{i,j\}$, $G$ is $F$ translated
by the local coordinate $i$; so the source-sink pair of $G$ is that of $F$
translated by $e_i$, and the two pairs are disjoint exactly when the source and
sink of $F$ are adjacent along $j$. A $2$-face of a unique sink orientation has
its source and sink adjacent along $j$ if and only if its two $i$-edges point in
opposite ways; so (T) on all faces containing $i$ says that the $i$-edge
orientation is constant on each of the two facets $\{v_i=0\}$, $\{v_i=1\}$,
which is uniformity of $i$. The statement about the outer coordinates is read
off the table of $O_{\alpha\beta}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[How high a Holt--Klee blow-up can go]\label{prop:hcube-blowbest}
Over every acyclic unique sink orientation of the $m$-cube for $m\le3$ --- one
representative of each of the $1$, $2$ and $18$ classes --- and every one of the
$2^{m}$ translation vectors $z$, the blow-ups $B(s,z)$ that are Holt--Klee have
greatest bottom-antipodal height
\[
  4,\qquad 6,\qquad 8 \qquad\text{at dimensions }3,\ 4,\ 5,
\]
attained by seeds of height $1$, $2$, $3$; in each case the value is $2h+2$ with
$h$ the greatest height of a parity-good seed of that dimension. Against
$h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}=4,6,11$ this means $B$ meets the Holt--Klee ceiling at
dimensions $3$ and $4$ and falls three short at dimension $5$; and over these
dimensions its growth inside the Holt--Klee class is $+2$ per dimension, that
is, linear. The twisted product of \Cref{lem:hstar-super} is no better: of the
$288$ twisted products of a $2$-cube orientation with a $3$-cube orientation,
$186$ are not Holt--Klee, and the tallest Holt--Klee one has height $5$; and
twisting the $1$-cube against the height-$11$ witness of
\Cref{prop:hcube-hkfive} gives a Holt--Klee orientation of the $6$-cube of
height at most $11$, attained only by the untwisted product.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:hcube-blow}
So the operation of \Cref{thm:blowup} leaves the Holt--Klee class for two
reasons at once, and \Cref{prop:D-quadratic}'s $D$ for the same reasons with
$z=\bar1$: the outer square reads the parity of the inner height, and a
$2$-face on which the parity is balanced with equal ends carries only two
disjoint monotone paths where three are needed; and the layer $(0,0)$ carries a
translate of the inner orientation, which on a $2$-face moves the source-sink
edge to the opposite edge of the square. The first obstruction is a property of
the seed alone, and \Cref{cor:hcube-parity} says every height-maximal seed at
$m\le4$ has it. This is why the search of \texttt{blowhk.py} over $B$'s rule
family found no Holt--Klee-preserving doubling: the parity readout, which is
what makes the walk turn round, is exactly what a $2$-face refuses. It does not
show that no dimension-raising doubling preserves Holt--Klee, and the numbers of
\Cref{prop:hcube-hkfive} leave room for one.
\end{remark}

\section{The positive direction}\label{sec:hcube-positive}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:hcube-positive}
What is proved above in the positive direction is \Cref{thm:hcube-dprod}: the
bottom-antipodal walk is linear in the dimension on LP orientations of deformed
products with factors of bounded dimension --- which is where the classical
lower-bound constructions live. Nothing here bounds the walk on a general LP
orientation of a cube, and nothing here bounds it on an occupancy polytope; in
particular \Cref{rem:hcube-notallcubes} shows the occupancy polytope of a
one-player game with a length-$6$ run at $m=4$ is not a deformed cube, so the
theorem does not reach the pivot. The honest statement is that the one-player
half of \Cref{cor:f-auso} --- equivalently, by \texttt{fs14:howard}, Howard's
rule on transient two-action Markov decision processes, the question
Melekopoglou and Condon leave open --- is not resolved here in either
direction, and that the standard geometric machinery cannot resolve it
negatively.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[The exact statements that are missing]\label{rem:hcube-gap}
Three, in increasing strength.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(G1)] $h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(m+2)\ge2h^{\ast}_{\mathrm{HK}}(m)+2$ for
  every $m\ge1$: that is, for every $m$ there is an operation taking a
  Holt--Klee acyclic unique sink orientation of the $m$-cube of maximal
  bottom-antipodal height to a Holt--Klee acyclic unique sink orientation of the
  $(m+2)$-cube of at least twice that height plus two. It holds for $m\le3$ by
  \Cref{prop:auso-census} and \Cref{prop:hcube-hkfive}, $11\ge2\cdot4+2$;
  \Cref{thm:blowup}'s $B$ does not witness it, by
  \Cref{cor:hcube-parity,cor:hcube-transl}, and no witness is known.
\item[\rm(G2)] Each of the five orientations of \Cref{rem:hcube-five} is, or is
  not, the orientation induced by a linear objective on a polytope
  combinatorially equivalent to the $4$-cube. This is a semialgebraic
  feasibility question in $m(2m+3)=44$ real unknowns, decidable in principle;
  a proof either way would be the first example, in this document, of a
  Holt--Klee orientation separated from the realisable ones, or of a proof that
  the two coincide at $m=4$.
\item[\rm(G3)] There is a family of nondegenerate one-player stopping simple
  stochastic games $G_m$ with $|\Vmax|=m$ whose all-switches runs have length
  superpolynomial in $m$. This is of the same strength as the open question of
  Melekopoglou and Condon and is not settled here.
\end{enumerate}
\end{remark}
